transcript: Does wicked for good address some of the plot holes from Wicked Act 2? This was one of my biggest questions going into the film, and unfortunately the answer is not really. Spoilers ahead, obviously, but some of the biggest critiques of Act 2 of wicked have to do with its timeline. For instance, we see Dorothy leave Munchkin land, and then fiyero comes in, gets captured by the guards, and taken out to the field where he will eventually become the Scarecrow. However, it is not clear how they actually get ahead of Dorothy on the yellow brick road, and the movie doesn't really address this either. They do sort of imply that they took horses, but it's not definitive. In the stage show, it is also unclear how Glinda gets to Kiamo Co, where Alpha Bet is hiding out at the end of the story. The movie once again gives the answer of a horse, which, yeah, sure, that's faster than walking. We still don't really know how she knew where to go, or how Darcy and the gang knew where to go for that matter, but we at least know how she got there. They also clarify where in the story March of the Witch Hunters takes place. In the film, they make it clear that it is after Darth and the gang have made it to the Wizard and asked him for help. It is still weirdly placed, and it's odd that they're forming this giant Mob and then just stop and let Darth and the gang go. And they're like, you guys got this. They also still don't do anything to address the very flimsy explanation given for why the lion doesn't like Alphabeta. They do add a scene earlier in the film where he explains himself a little bit more and talks about how he heard a rumor that she was the one who gave the monkeys their wings. But it's still not a very compelling reason. And if anything, I actually like the musical's explanation better, because in the musical, the lion is too scared to say anything in front of the crowd, so buck has to speak for him, which could be interpreted as buck bringing in his own biases against Alpha. And this isn't actually emblematic of how the lion feels, but the film kind of confirms that, no, that is how he feels. And I don't know, even with the additional context, I still don't quite buy it. And. And another plot hole that they don't address at all is how the Ruby slippers have the power to bring Dorothy home. And also, how did Glinda know that they have that power? It's not really addressed at all in the musical, and it's not addressed in the movie either. No, I don't think that wicked the movie or the musical is a bad because of these plot holes. I think what wicked for good proves is you kind of need These plot holes in order for the story to function. And they're a little bit of a necessary evil in order to get characters in the places that you need them to be. And so while I was a little bit disappointed that they weren't able to address them more thoroughly, it didn't really detract from my enjoyment of the film at all.
